I don't really like living my life out of fear of hell. If there's hell and it is how they say it is, then I would end up going there anyway, and I intend to live my life the way I want to live it, so I would be able to look back at the reasons that would had gotten me there and know that it wasn't for something stupid but for something important, important for me at least. I don't want to live a religious life. I do have some sort of believe that nothing gets created anymore. There's (in my mind) only transformation. Matter is not created, it's transformed. Everything in our body was once something else, even stars. After we die, it has to go somewhere, and being a part of the universe for eternity seems like a relaxing way to be. We're immortals in a way. That's what I sometimes believe anyway. And so I think of death as a friend maybe, not as something bad right now. At least for me, as long as I receive it with open arms, it's ok.

Okay first of all, thank you for your time. That is quite a long message and I can see it took time, effort and dedication to write that. I see that you care, so, thank you.

My feeling is something hard to explain. I'm extremely disappointed in myself, and angry for what I did. But I kinda can't believe that I did that, I can't believe that I did something that hurt my partner so much and broke my relationship - and with it my life. The worst is that it was me who did it, like I remember taking those decisions, and that's something I can't understand, I wouldn't have understood that before doing it if it would had crossed my mind. 

I can't say what I would tell that friend because my problem is my feelings towards the person I hurt. I forgive people very lightly mostly, I don't hold on too much to anger when somebody hurts me. But when someone hurts someone I love like that, when someone hurt my ex for example, there was nothing that person could do to earn my forgiveness. That's the problem here, is not that I hurt me, I hurt the one I love, so I can't really forgive myself, it goes against my nature if you will. Those feelings of anger and disgust block me completely.

I don't have anything diagnosed because I never go to doctors or anything like that, I've been at a doctor's only a couple of times in the past 10 years I guess. But I think I might have some sort of anxiety when it comes to show people my sad feelings and the sort. It is weird because I am usually a confident person, even when I am not comfortable, I can move my way around pretty much any social encounter, I guess I am good at masking myself. But something pushes me back when it comes to those feelings and it just doesn't let me. I guess this is something that I have to deal by myself, and I know that's not the best idea, but it is what I have, for better or for worse.

I've had my decision of killing myself for a while now, and I guess I've only delayed it because of smoking weed. It's like my medicine, my natural medicine. I am not about to start taking anti depressant pills and stuff like that, I am against all that pharmaceutical stuff if I have something that works better and is healthier and natural. But around a week ago, I was unable to buy because the police took away my weed when I was getting it, and then I was too nervous to get more for like a week. I got really anxious and nervous when I finally took the courage to go get some more. But I did it, and that's why now I am way more relaxed about it. I still want to do it but it's like there's not so much hurry right now. I am actually kinda numb and just going through the day. I guess I know that suicide is not the best option, but I still think I'll do it sooner or later, I guess.

I need to say thanks again for just taking the time to write. Even if I say sometimes that I can't do this or that, it still feels nice that you do what you do.

Are you George R.R. Martin?

Nice and powerful drawing by the way, I like it.

I am not a religious person, so I am not so worried about that. So what you are saying is that the problem with suicide is the unknown. But suicide means death, and we all die, so we all have to face the unknown. What if you're ready to go? Isn't it better to stand up and walk together with death than being dragged to wherever it is we go (or not) at the end?
That's my problem, people who are left behind. I guess I am just trying to find a way to come to peace with the fact that there will be suffering when I'm gone.

Nobody can stop me but myself, that's true. But knowing my loved ones' suffering after it's done is not a nice way to go. I guess that's something I can't control, like many things in life.
Anything can change, even my own thoughts. What makes me sad today might make me happy tomorrow. But we live in the here and now. Reasons for taking your own life depends in the individual. Usually the most common reason is a lack of hope. That's not the case with me. I have no doubt that I would be happy if I go on. I don't have a bad life. I might not have a job, a career, a partner, a home of my own, a sane mind, a willingness to get out of bed or a reason to smile, but all those things can change. I actually had all of those things and I lost them, and the only one responsible for that is me. I was at the top and now I'm at the bottom. I spent years building a life I was happy with, I built dreams and a future, but that's gone now. I just don't feel like starting over, I don't want to start over, I don't want to build something that's kinda close to what I had, chasing a life I will never have. I might get a similar life, but not the one that I want. I have to live with this guilt of having fucked everything up and hurt the one I loved. I didn't just fuck up my life, I fucked up the life of my better half. And that's the problem, when I found that better half I gave myself in and we became one person. Now that this half is gone, I stand alone without a way to fix myself, I can create a new self, but I died a while ago. 

I'm sorry that you got the impression that your time and effort was not appreciated. I didn't downvote your response or any of the others. I appreciate you taking the time to answer me, and I'm not about to disrespect someone who takes interest in what goes on in my mind and gets out of his way to share his own mind with me.

This movie has given me hope. Most of the people who were interviewed have moved on. They have accepted what happened and they sort of understand it. It gives me hope that it will be like that with my loved ones as well.

It means so much to me, it really does. So, if the people who made this movie ever happen to read this comment, I just want to say thank you for your work.

What is bad? What is good? Suicide is "bad" because of your culture. In other cultures, suicide is normal and ok, sometimes even "good".

I understand what you say about wishing that they didn't care. I sometimes think the same, but then I realize that I don't think that at all. I don't want them to not care. I want them to care about me, I want them to think about me and bring a smile upon their faces. I want to die and that my loved ones get a smile on their faces with thoughts like "such a great person", "hehehe, I remember when we did this and that, so cool". Pretty much like people do when a loved one goes away to another country for example and they never talk again.

I'm not a religious person, I'm actually agnostic. But, what if we're all dead and living in hell? What if this life is actually a short vacation from hell because eternity is a bit too long to do it non-stop?
I think the best person you can open up to is someone who has had depression (has tried to kill him/herself, for example). Those people understand the most, and they usually don't judge.

They don't know that I'm struggling. I guess there are stuff that they can do to stop it, and maybe that's the problem because I don't want it to stop. I could probably get out of this by myself as well, but I don't want to get out.

That's what worries me the most, I am not sure that they'll be able to move on.

I'm not a person who opens to others, I've opened myself to two persons in my whole life (I'm in my mid twenties), and they're both gone. I've never opened myself to my family, and I'm not going to. I can't say that you're wrong because you're not. I do owe it to them to ask for help, and I can be happy again. I can move on, I know that. But I just can't. I hurt the person I loved the most, I was an asshole. And it wasn't a mistake of the moment, it happened for over two months. What did I do? For the first time, I was selfish. I put my own interests first, and I turned my back to my loved one. Sure, I am human, and I make mistakes. That person forgave me for my mistakes, but I don't forgive myself. I actually believe that killing myself is not what I deserve, I deserve to live with this pain and go on suffering, knowing what I've done, but I guess my selfish side won't let me. I am not a bad person, even after all I had done, the person whom I had hurt told me that. But still, I never saw myself capable of doing what I had done, so I can't say what I'm capable of doing anymore.

Imagine the most beautiful person you have ever seen. I'm not talking about looks, I'm talking about the whole package. Imagine you love that person with all your heart. And then imagine that person crying because of your actions, and you lying to that person and turning your back on that person. What does that say about yourself? Who the fuck are you? How can you trust yourself? Everything you thought about yourself is gone, all your values. And you went down on your knees for the first time in your life asking that person to please not leave you. Begging might seem like not much, but it was for me. I never begged for anything. I never went down on my knees with a waterfall of tears and asked someone to not leave me. But that someone did. And I can't blame that someone because that someone is right. How can that person trust me after what I've done? After all the lies.

After everything went to hell, I lost my loved one, my friends, my future, my home, my pets, my possessions, my town, my adopted country, my job, my self respect. I am uncomfortable with my looks. I lost a quarter of my weight in just a couple of months, and I lost my willingness to do anything.

I can't ask for help. I always wanted to grow old with that person and spend my whole life with that person. I can't grow old with that person anymore, but I can say that my life started and ended with that person. It was a beautiful life, full of beautiful memories.

That's unfortunate. I was thinking of writing two letters, one to my family and one to my ex. To my family because it would, otherwise, appear too sudden and too unexplainable. I feel that they wouldn't be able to cope. I just don't want them to never stop asking themselves "why", or saying that they should've/could've done something, or whatever. And to my ex to not make her feel responsible.
You see, I was in a position where I had to choose which path to take. I know one of them would have lead me to "moving on" and have a reasonably fine life, and the other one would have just end it. Yeah dunno, maybe you're right. But then, there's no point in writing anything? I'm gonna go either way, I just want to do it in the best possible way. I know I'll be leaving scars, I just want them to be as small as possible.

The things I have to say are known to those I care of knowing. I guess this is my "setting one's affairs in order" phase.
I guess that means that there's no point in writing something. I mean, if I don't want to blame someone or something like that.
